title: Steam's tidying game trend is about to get the haunted meat it's been missing
summary: Something is Wrong with the Library is bringing some much-needed texture to organizing sims.
body: What happened: I Am Your Beast and Clickolding developer Strange Scaffold has announced Something is Wrong with the Library , a tidying game set in "a library haunted by blood and meat." Players will both reshelve the library's scattered books with a real Dewey Decimal System implementation while facing the accursed energies emanating from the corpses its billionaire patron entombed in the walls . A "Modular Chaos System" ensures each playthrough has its own set of books to reorganize. There's at least one terrifying, inscrutable obelisk. Something is Wrong with the Library is set to launch before the end of 2026. It's nice to see some aura in the tidying space In recent months, Steam has been awash in organize-em-ups and haystack searchers —games capitalizing on the simple pleasure of arranging a chaotic melange into an orderly assemblage. But while I'd never think to deny the meditative appeal of putting a thing in a place, I'm not going to pretend that the emergent craze isn't undergoing the same gold rush of low-effort iteration that we saw during the rash of retail sims. title: Embark should've implemented a PvE mode into Arc Raiders a long time ago
summary: God forbid a raider wants to have a chill time.
body: I am very excited at the prospect of an Arc Raiders PvE-only mode. I have been ever since I got a tiny taste of what it could be like in Shared Watch , and even before that while playing in friendly lobbies. I know some aren't happy at the prospect of a mode with no PvP, but the only thing I can't believe is that Embark hasn't made this change sooner. I've always thought that Arc Raiders was at its best in its early stages when players had to work together to take down high-value arcs. This kind of cooperation led to some genuinely hilarious scenarios or just nice encounters with strangers; something I hadn't experienced in an online multiplayer game for quite some time. (Image credit: Embark Studios) At one point I remember being huddled in a bunker with another trio while trying to take down a Rocketeer on Spaceport. While we did manage to kill it, we were then caught out when a second Rocketeer turned up and we had almost no ammo left. It was a slightly bizarre situation to be found in with strangers. title: A love letter to the Guitar Hero X-Plorer Controller
summary: Simply the best.
body: I peaked at 16 years old. I was part way through an expert run of 'Through the Fire and the Flames' by Dragonforce on Guitar Hero 3 at a friend's house for their birthday, and I remember thinking to myself, 'I don't think I'll ever top this'. As the song came to an end and I revelled in my passing grade, I got at least one nod of approval from the group before they slunk off to do what actually cool 16-year-olds do when presented with a free house and no adults around: smoke a big joint. I've given it my all, on that same 20-year-old X-Plorer, with one of my favourite songs from that time. Scroll down for my cool video. Not me, though. I got high on sweet riffs, adeptly played out across five colourful buttons, slapped in near-perfect rhythm alongside a singular strum bar. Learn a real guitar? No, thanks. title: Between 70 and 80% of Blood Bowl 3 games were solo
summary: Improving the new version's AI is a priority.
body: You'll know this frustration if you've ever been part of the community around a game that has both singleplayer and multiplayer modes. People who prefer one to the other are always convinced the other cohort doesn't exist. "Nobody plays this game in a different way to me and my friends, and anyone who says they do is lying." In the case of the Blood Bowl videogames, the fact the CPU's tactics are so rudimentary has always given people who prefer the multiplayer mode ammunition for claiming the other half doesn't exist. Now we've got proof they're actually the majority. As Cyanide programmer Mathieu Valero recently told Wargamer , between 70 and 80% of Blood Bowl 3 games were played solo in Eternal Leagues. This came up in the context of Blood Bowl 3's imminent replacement by Warhammer Blood Bowl. One of the improvements, Valero suggests, will be the AI. "We didn't have an AI—now we do", as he put it. "There are still a bunch of factions and builds that it's more able to play well: you want to give it Guard and Block, and don't go fancy with the combos that a human would be able to do", he went on to say, but "give something reliable to the AI, and you're gonna have a game to play"…

body: Tom's Hardware and Respawn First recently reported on a fun new patent from those wiz kids at Microsoft, one that would dynamically pause your game to show you advertisements. Here are the big wham lines from the abstract of US 202610260258 A1 , "Contextually Aware Management of Interactive Software Application Access:" "A content management system may suspend a user's interaction with the interactive software application based on the promoted content trigger event." (Emphasis mine) "A content management system may present the promoted audiovisual content to the user." "A content management system may establish a credit … the credit delays suspension of the user's interaction." That's the sort of whimsical creativity that made me fall in love with games in the first place. In plain English: This is a system for showing advertisements during gameplay, one that pauses your game (suspends your interaction).
